messages.subject: SSM estimate gives very high standard deviation
messages.subject_clean: SSM estimate gives very high standard deviation
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to make a simulate a simple SSM

I(t+1) | N(t) ~ Normal(N(t),sigma)

N(t+1) | N(t) ~ Normal(N(t),tau)

N(0) ~ Normal(0,tau)

then estimate it using TMB. But the deviation estimate from TMB is very large. Below is the model specification in C++.

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  DATA_VECTOR(I);
  PARAMETER(tau);
  PARAMETER(sigma);
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(N);

  Type nll;

  nll = 0;
  nll += pow(N[0],2)/(2*pow(tau,2));

  for (int t = 1; t < N.size(); ++t)
  {
    nll += pow(N[t]-N[t-1],2)/(2*pow(tau,2));
    nll += pow(I[t-1]-N[t],2)/(2*pow(sigma,2));
  }

  return nll;
}

The standard deviation estimate is as below. The true standard deviation I specified was 1. But the estimate gives 8.266817e+18. Hessian is not positive definite either - which I think it should be since the objective is convex.

          Estimate Std. Error
tau   8.266817e+18        NaN
sigma 8.177680e+18        NaN
Warning:
Hessian of fixed effects was not positive definite.
Maximum gradient component: 6.666656e-18

R code is as below.

setwd('/Users/garyzhu/Desktop/popSSM/gary/gary_code/tmb_explorer')
compile("llm_hc.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("llm_hc"))

set.seed(0)
T = 100
N = rep(0,T)
tau = 1
sigma = 1
N[1] = rnorm(1,0,tau)
for (t in 2:T) {
  N[t] = rnorm(1,N[t-1],tau)
}
I = rnorm(N[2:T],sigma)
I
N

obj = MakeADFun(data=list('I'=I),parameters=list('tau'=tau,'sigma'=sigma,'N'=N),random='N',DLL='llm_hc')
opt = nlminb(start=obj$par,obj=obj$fn,gr=obj$gr,control=list(eval.max=5000,iter.max=5000))

rep = sdreport(obj)
summary.rep = summary(rep)

rep
summary.rep

est.tau = summary.rep[1,1]
est.sigma = summary.rep[2,1]
est.N = summary.rep[3:nrow(summary.rep),1]

plot = ggplot() +
  labs(color='') +
  geom_line(aes(x=1:T,y=N,color='true')) +
  geom_line(aes(x=1:T,y=est.N,color='predicted')) +
  xlab('year') +
  ylab('index')
plot

messages.body_plain:
Hi Gary,

The estimates are incorrect because the -log(tau) and -log(sigma) are missing in the densities for the negative log-likelihood. I pasted my C++ code below. Also, I recommend using the standard deviations in the log-scale. You can use ADREPORT in the C++ code and summary(rep, select="report") to return the estimates in the original scale. I obtain the estimates below but the estimate for tau is still off. Increasing the length of N result in smaller estimates of tau and not the true 1. To obtain the tau used to generate the data, I think you will need to sample many samples o f N, not increase the length of N. Can anyone with knowledge of SSM help?

Hope this helps,

Kyaw Sint (Joe)

> summary(rep, select="report")
       Estimate Std. Error
tau   0.1394212 0.05519153
sigma 0.9526566 0.07388882

#include <TMB.hpp>

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator

() ()
{
  DATA_VECTOR(I);
  PARAMETER(logtau);
  PARAMETER(logsigma);
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(N);

  Type nll;

  Type tau = exp(logtau);
  Type sigma = exp(logsigma);

  nll = 0;

  //nll += pow(N[0],2)/(2*pow(tau,2));
  nll -= -0.5 * pow(N[0]/tau,2) - log(sqrt(2*M_PI)) - logtau;

for (int t = 1

; t < N.size(); ++t)
  {
    //nll += pow(N[t]-N[t-1],2)/(2*pow(tau,2));
    //nll += pow(I[t-1]-N[t],2)/(2*pow(sigma,2));
    nll -= -0.5 * pow((N[t]-N[t-1])/tau,2) - log(sqrt(2*M_PI)) - logtau;
    nll -= -0.5 * pow((I[t-1]-N[t])/sigma,2) - log(sqrt(2*M_PI)) - logsigma;
  }

  ADREPORT(tau)
  ADREPORT(sigma)

  return nll;
}

#include <TMB.hpp>

  PARAMETER(sigma);
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(N);

  nll = 0.0;

messages.body_plain:
This is the plot I generated

I'm using the code

#include <TMB.hpp>

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  DATA_VECTOR(I);

  PARAMETER(rho);
  PARAMETER(tau);
  PARAMETER(sigma);

  PARAMETER_VECTOR(N);

  Type nll = 0.0;

  nll += pow(N[0],2)/(2*pow(tau,2))+log(tau);

  for (int t = 1; t < N.size(); ++t)
  {

    nll += pow(N[t]-rho*N[t-1],2)/(2*pow(tau,2))+log(tau);
    nll += pow(I[t-1]-N[t],2)/(2*pow(sigma,2))+log(sigma);
  }

  ADREPORT(rho);
  ADREPORT(tau);
  ADREPORT(sigma);

  REPORT(rho);
  REPORT(tau);
  REPORT(sigma);

  return nll;
}

and

#//////////////////////////////
#### simple SSM hard-coded ####
#//////////////////////////////

require(TMB)
require(ggplot2)

setwd('/Users/garyzhu/Desktop/popSSM/gary/gary_code/tmb_explorer')
compile("llm_hc.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("llm_hc"))

set.seed(0)
T = 100
N = rep(0,T)
tau = 1

sigma = 0.3
rho = 0.5

N[1] = rnorm(1,0,tau)
for (t in 2:T) {

  N[t] = rnorm(1,rho * N[t-1],tau)

}
I = rnorm(N[2:T],sigma)
I
N

obj = MakeADFun(data=list('I'=I),

                parameters=list(rho=rho,
                                tau=tau,
                                sigma=sigma,
                                N=N),
                random='N',

                DLL='llm_hc')
opt = nlminb(start=obj$par,obj=obj$fn,gr=obj$gr,control=list(eval.max=5000,iter.max=5000))

sdr = sdreport(obj)
summary.rep.fixed = summary(sdr,"fixed")
summary.rep.random = summary(sdr,"random")

est.rho = summary.rep.fixed[dimnames(summary.rep.fixed)[[1]]=='rho',1]
est.tau = summary.rep.fixed[dimnames(summary.rep.fixed)[[1]]=='tau',1]
est.sigma = summary.rep.fixed[dimnames(summary.rep.fixed)[[1]]=='sigma',1]
est.N = summary.rep.random[dimnames(summary.rep.random)[[1]]=='N',1]

plot = ggplot() +
  labs(color='') +
  geom_line(aes(x=1:T,y=N,color='true')) +
  geom_line(aes(x=1:T,y=est.N,color='predicted')) +
  xlab('year') +
  ylab('index')
plot

Clearly the prediction is quite far-off.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Gary,

Using log scale is better for numerical stability.  Software also throw an error if you give a negative value to the log function which could occur during the calculations. Another common problem I have encountered is division by zero and exponentiating to very large or small numbers.

>From your plot, my intuition is that your model is using the previous N and not considering other previous N. Can you apply a correlation structure in a SSM model? Check the multivariate distributions and autoregressive processes chapter in the TMB documentation https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/_book/Densities.html

Kyaw Sint (Joe)
